blocks.text: Commentary & Market Overview
Final Close

items: Guggenheim Investments Private Debt Fund IV (‘PDF IV’ or ‘The Fund’) held its final close on March 31, 2026. The Fund closed on $4.5 billion in commitments.

blocks.text: Market Backdrop

items: After a robust start to the year, volumes fell sharply in Q2: US direct-lending volumes dropped roughly 55% quarter-on-quarter from $74.7bn in Q1 to $33.6bn in Q2, the lowest quarterly print since Q2 2023, with deal count falling in line from 217 in Q1 to 154 in Q21.

Credit stress remains overall contained but became more visible in H1 2026: Fitch's US Private Credit Default Rate hit a record 6.1% LTM through July 2026, though ~88% of default events were PIK swaps, payment deferrals, or maturity extensions rather than bankruptcies2. BDC non-accrual rates drifted higher through Q2 2026 with widening manager dispersion, reaching a median ~2.5% at cost across KBRA's rated BDC universe (up from ~1.9% two quarters earlier)3.

Volatility in the first half of the year, driven by software/AI credit concerns, heightened geopolitical uncertainty, and retail-vehicle outflows (redemption pressure on semi-liquid BDCs and interval funds), triggered a short-term pullback in deployment across the market. At the same time, these forces have improved the technical backdrop and have supported a lender-friendly reset for patient managers: less capital is competing per deal, market data indicates that H1 2026 spreads broadly have moved wider than late-2025 levels, and the resulting technical environment promotes stronger risk-adjusted returns.

Software volumes dropped sharply in H1 2026. Among a composite of the 12 largest BDCs, software loans represent ~30% of exposure1, compared to 18% of PDF IV (15% pro-forma signed deals which will close imminently). PDF IV’s software loans continue to perform in line with expectation without credit concerns.

blocks.text: PDF IV Recent Activity

items: Consistent with our process over the last 20+ years, we remain focused on finding compelling relative value in fundamentally sound companies.

There are two names that we have added to our ‘Monitor List’. Inspired Pet Nutrition (added last quarter) where 2Q26 performance remains softer than budgeted with weaker UK volume trends and increased rate of trade discounts provided impacting margins. Management expects performance to improve in 2H26 and into 2027 aided by new contracts secured in the UK and the majority of French synergy initiatives were executed in 2Q26. We have also added AtHome to our Monitor List following a coordinated estate agent federation campaign that has cost customers and stalled planned price increases. We are monitoring via direct management engagement (a recent on-site in Luxembourg covering a corrective action plan, new pricing designed with the Sponsor and advisors, plus product development to lift agent and buyer engagement) all of these factors encourage that similar disputes have been navigated in the UK, New Zealand, and the Baltics. We do not view our loan as near impaired in either case, but we are focused on both names given the recent softness.

Beyond heightened monitoring in AtHome and IPN, all PDF IV assets are performing well and in line with or above financial/operating plans. Three loans are currently electing PIK alongside cash coupon (all of which is designed PIK at origination whereby there is a clear path to sunset over time). PIK as a percentage of net investment income (NII) in PDF IV remains less than 2%, compared to 21.0% PIK as a share of NII among a composite of the 12 largest US BDCs4.

PDF IV closed five deals in 2Q26. Since the end of the second quarter, PDF IV has closed an additional five deals and has signed another incremental four deals which will close shortly. Year to date, the closed deals represent $1.3bn of dollars committed at a weighted average spread of SOFR + 539 basis points with first lien net leverage of 4.2x, a blended LTV of 42% and meaningful downside and structural protections in each of these deals.
Please see the enclosed case studies for additional information on the deals closed in 2Q26. There were no portfolio realizations or exits in 2Q26.

blocks.text: Guggenheim Communication: Clarification on Recent Media Coverage

items: Additionally, we want to address recent media coverage concerning Guggenheim Investments, TWG and its affiliated insurance companies, Delaware Life and Clear Spring. Guggenheim Investments and Guggenheim Corporate Funding (the entity that manages PDF IV), are separate and distinct from, and are not affiliates of, TWG or its insurance companies, and the investigation involving related party or affiliate transactions among TWG and its insurance companies does not involve Guggenheim Investments or Guggenheim Corporate Funding. From the perspective of PDF IV and the broader private debt platform, it is business as usual, with investment processes, portfolio management, and day-to-day operations continuing uninterrupted as we remain focused on deploying capital into high-quality opportunities. We are committed to maintaining an open dialogue as the situation evolves, will provide further updates as appropriate, and welcome any questions in the meantime. 1.
